newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's JSE says market closed for Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's JSE says market closed for Wednesday.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said on Wednesday the market had been closed for the day after a total of just 27 minutes of trade due to system problems.
Trade was re-opened at 1320 GMT after earlier system problems, but another system failure led to the closure of trade after only 10 minutes.

"During November 27, 1996 the JSE JET system was opened on two occasions for trading. On both occasions brokers experienced delayed response times and inadequate performance on their trading screens," the JSE said in a statement.
He said total trade was 208.3 million rand, about 40 percent of a normal day's trade.

The exchange said technicians from Chicago, the suppliers of the system, were on site carrying out a thorough diagnostic analysis of the system. Brokers had also been asked to staff their terminals at 0530 GMT on Thursday in the event that further tests were necessary.
The system failed twice on Monday after the installation of of new software at the weekend and the opening was delayed for an hour on Tuesday.
JSE president Roy Andersen said the delays experienced over the past few days were of concern to the exchange.
